messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
   Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

## Command Execution Rules

You are operating in an environment where

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

Each response should include:

1. **Reasoning text** where you explain your analysis and plan
2. At least one tool call with your command

**CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

- Your response SHOULD include reasoning text explaining what you're doing
- Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call
- Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell.
- However, you can prefix any action with `MY_ENV_VAR=MY_VALUE cd /path/to/working/dir && ...` or write/load environment variables from files
- Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.

# Replace only first occurrence

# Replace first occurrence on line 1
sed -i '1s/old_string/new_string/' filename.py

# Replace all occurrences in lines 1-10

# Chat Bots Architecture

## Data Model
Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (`User::Role`), implemented via the `User::Bot` concern:
- `users.bot_token`: unique random token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`) generated on create for bots; `nil` for human users and deactivated bots.
- `users.creator_id`: references the `User` who created the bot, allowing `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` to work uniformly for creators and administrators.
- `users.webhook_url`: optional HTTP/HTTPS URL where the bot receives mention callbacks. Blank values normalize to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook.
- `bot_key` (`"<id>-<bot_token>"`): the credential displayed in the UI ("Bot code") and used in the messaging API URL. Verified with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Reusing `User` means bots automatically inherit:
  - Open-room auto-join (`after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open`)

# Chat Bots Architecture

## Data Model
Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (`User::Role`), implemented via the `User::Bot` concern:
- `users.bot_token`: unique random token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`) generated on create for bots; `nil` for human users and deactivated bots.
- `users.creator_id`: references the `User` who created the bot, allowing `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` to work uniformly for creators and administrators.
- `users.webhook_url`: optional HTTP/HTTPS URL where the bot receives mention callbacks. Blank values normalize to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook.
- `bot_key` (`"<id>-<bot_token>"`): the credential displayed in the UI ("Bot code") and used in the messaging API URL. Verified with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Reusing `User` means bots automatically inherit:
  - Open-room auto-join (`after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open`)
  - Closed-room membership management (`Rooms::ClosedsController`)
  - `@`-mention autocompletion (`Autocompletable::UsersController`) and `Message#mentionees` resolution
  - Message authorship (`messages.creator_id`), avatars (`User::Avatar`), broadcasts (`Message::Broadcasts`), and push notifications (`Room::MessagePusher`)
- Bots are excluded from human-only surfaces (login, session transfers, account member list, sidebar DM placeholders) via `User.not_bot`.
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil` and `webhook_url: nil`, and removes all memberships while preserving historical messages.

## Routes & Controllers
- `BotsController` (`resources :bots, except: :show`): UI for listing (`/bots`), creating (`/bots/new`), editing (`/bots/:id/edit`), and deleting bots. Linked from `/account/edit` ("Set up chat bots") for all members. The form includes the optional `Webhook URL` field (`bot[webhook_url]`).
- `Bots::MessagesController` (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`): unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint reading raw request body (or `params[:attachment]`) and returning `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`, `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, or `401 Unauthorized`.

## Outbound Webhooks (`Bot::Webhook` & `Bot::WebhookJob`)
- When a message is created (`after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_bot_webhooks_later` finds active, mentioned bots in that room that have a `webhook_url` (excluding `message.creator`) and enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per bot.
- Enqueueing per-bot background jobs ensures webhook HTTP calls never block the user posting the message or delay other bots.
- `Bot::Webhook` posts `Content-Type: application/json` with:
  - `event`: `"mention"`
  - `author`: `{ id, name }`
  - `room`: `{ id, name, reply_to }` (`reply_to` is the relative `room_bot_messages_path` for that room & bot)
  - `message`: `{ id, body: { text, html }, link }` (`link` is the relative `room_at_message_path`)
- `message.body.text` strips only the target bot's own `<action-text-attachment>` mention node(s) using a unique sentinel before converting to plain text, handling both ASCII spaces and ` ` (`\u00A0`) while preserving other users' and bots' `@`-mentions.
- Synchronous responses:
  - `200` with `text/plain` (HTML-escaped so literal text renders safely) or `text/html` posts the non-blank response body into the room as the bot's message and calls `broadcast_create`.
  - `204` (or other statuses / empty body) posts nothing.
- Outbound webhook URLs intentionally permit `http://` and `https://` on localhost and private networks (unlike `Opengraph::Fetch`) so self-hosted Campfire instances and local integrations/tests can target internal services.

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_bot_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_bot_webhooks_later(message)
      message.mentionees.with_webhook.where.not(id: message.creator_id).find_each do |bot|
        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, message)
      end
    end

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_bot_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_bot_webhooks_later(message)
      message.mentionees.with_webhook.where.not(id: message.creator_id).find_each do |bot|
        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, message)
      end
    end
end

class BotsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  test "account edit shows Set up chat bots link to all members" do
    get edit_account_url
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "a[href='#{bots_path}']", text: /Set up chat bots/
    assert_select "a[href='#{edit_account_custom_styles_path}']", count: 0

    sign_in :david
    get edit_account_url
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "a[href='#{bots_path}']", text: /Set up chat bots/
    assert_select "a[href='#{edit_account_custom_styles_path}']", text: /Custom styles/
  end

  test "bots do not appear in account users list" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Hidden From People Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))

    sign_in :david
    get edit_account_url
    assert_response :ok
    assert_no_match /Hidden From People Bot/, response.body

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { delete account_user_url(bot) }
  end

  test "index requires authentication" do
    delete session_url
    get bots_url
    assert_redirected_to new_session_url
  end

  test "member sees only bots they created, admin sees all bots" do
    kevins_bot = User.create!(name: "Kevin Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    jzs_bot = User.create!(name: "JZ Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:jz))

    get bots_url
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "li", text: /Kevin Bot/ do
      assert_select "label", text: "Bot code"
      assert_select "input[readonly][value='#{kevins_bot.bot_key}']"
      assert_select "a[href='#{edit_bot_path(kevins_bot)}']", text: /Edit Kevin Bot/
    end
    assert_no_match /JZ Bot/, response.body
    assert_select "a[href='#{new_bot_path}']", text: /Add a chat bot/

    sign_in :david
    get bots_url
    assert_response :ok
    assert_match /Kevin Bot/, response.body
    assert_match /JZ Bot/, response.body
  end

  test "index renders all bots without pagination" do
    25.times { |i| User.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin)) }

    get bots_url
    assert_response :ok
    25.times { |i| assert_match /Bot #{i}/, response.body }
  end

  test "new renders form with required name, optional avatar, optional Webhook URL, and Save changes button" do
    get new_bot_url
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "form[action='#{bots_path}']" do
      assert_select "input[type='file'][name='bot[avatar]']"
      assert_select "input[name='bot[name]'][required][placeholder='Name the bot']"
      assert_select "label", text: /Webhook URL/ do
        assert_select "input[type='url'][name='bot[webhook_url]'][placeholder='Webhook URL']:not([required])"
      end
      assert_select "button[type='submit']", text: /Save changes/
    end
  end

  test "create creates bot with optional webhook_url, joins open rooms, and redirects to bots index" do
    assert_difference -> { User.active.bot.count }, 1 do
      post bots_url, params: {
        bot: {

**Analyzing the Membership Logic**

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. The goal is to ensure bots no longer automatically join open rooms unless specifically configured to do so, while people continue to have the existing behavior. I need to be precise and account for every edge case, especially considering how the existing system works.

First, I need to identify *all* the places where the system currently handles user (and now bot) membership in open rooms. There are two primary locations to examine: `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` (triggered after a user's creation) and `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users` (triggered after an open room is created or converted).

*   **`User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`:** For *people*, everything remains the same: they join open rooms upon creation. However, for bots, I need a new attribute, let's call it `"Add to all open rooms"` (as a switch), which, if set to `true`, *should* cause the bot to join all open rooms at creation. If the switch is off (default), the bot doesn't join any open rooms. *Critically*, if a bot *does* have the switch enabled at creation, I need to ensure the joined webhooks are triggered.

*   **`Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users`:** This is where it gets interesting, and potentially tricky. When a *new* open room is created, or a closed room is converted to open, the existing code automatically grants access to *all* active users (`User.active`). I need to modify this behavior to account for the new "Add to all open rooms" switch on bots.
    *   People (`User.active.not_bot`) should still automatically get added to new or converted open rooms.
    *   Bots should *only* be added to new or converted open rooms if their "Add to all open rooms" switch is turned ON. If the switch is OFF, they must not be added, and *no* webhook trigger.
    *   I need to be very careful here. The existing transaction within `Room.create_for` already grants memberships and then the `after_save_commit` calls run. So `memberships.grant_to(Current.user)` will add the user inside the transaction, and the `after_save_commit` call of `memberships.grant_to(User.active)` will run after, adding everyone. I need to figure out how to filter this correctly. Since there's a unique index on `[room_id, user_id]`, I can ignore the possibility of duplicate entries - though I'll need to confirm that `insert_all` handles that correctly, with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.

*   **UI Concerns:** I need to make sure the UI reflects these changes. The bot form (new and edit) requires a new switch for "Add to all open rooms." This switch must default to "off." I also need to verify what user listings are displayed in open room forms to reflect the correct people/bots. I'll need to make sure the open room views in `Rooms::OpensController#new` and `#edit` show the correct users (or, likely, a more restricted set based on membership or "add to open rooms" state).

    * I need to carefully verify that `User.active` appropriately scopes to exclude inactive users, but include bots with the proper switch setting.

class Bots::MessagesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    host! "once.campfire.test"
    @bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david))
    @room = rooms(:hq)
  end

  test "posting a raw text message creates message, returns 201 with Location, broadcasts, and pushes" do
    assert_difference -> { @room.messages.count }, 1 do
      assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts [ @room, :messages ], count: 1 do
        assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(users(:kevin).id), 1 do
          assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Room::PushMessageJob do
            post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅"
          end
        end
      end
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_equal message_path(message), response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert_equal "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅", message.plain_text_body

    # Verify rendered room shows bot name as author
    sign_in :kevin
    get room_url(@room)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "##{dom_id(message)}" do
      assert_select ".message__author", text: /Deploy Bot/
      assert_match /Deploy of v1\.2\.3 finished ✅/, response.body
    end
  end

  test "posting a message triggers web push notifications with bot name" do
    task_count = Push::Subscription.count - users(:kevin).push_subscriptions.count
    # hq has david, jason, jz, kevin (plus @bot who has 0 subscriptions).
    # In fixtures, let's check how many push subscriptions belong to hq members:
    expected_deliveries = Push::Subscription.joins(user: :memberships)
      .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: @room).where.not(user: @bot))
      .merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
      .count

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(expected_deliveries).with do |message:, **|
        payload = JSON.parse(message)
        payload["title"] == @room.name && payload.dig("options", "body") == "Deploy Bot: Build green"
      end

      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Build green", headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "text/plain" }
      assert_response :created
    end

    pool = Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.delivery_pool
    start = Time.now
    while pool.completed_task_count < expected_deliveries
      raise "Timeout waiting for pool tasks" if Time.now - start > 0.5
      sleep 0.01
    end
  end

  test "posting special characters with curl-style form content-type preserves raw body" do
    raw = "Build 100% done & ready=true\nNext line"
    post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key),
      params: raw,
      headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created
    message = @room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_equal raw, message.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting with attachment succeeds" do
    assert_difference -> { @room.messages.count }, 1 do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { attachment: fixture_file_upload("earth.png", "image/png") }
    end

    assert_response :created
    message = @room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_equal message_path(message), response.headers["Location"]
    assert message.attachment?
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
  end

  test "empty body and no attachment returns 422 Unprocessable Content" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key)
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key), params: "   "
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@room, @bot.bot_key),
        params: { not_an_attachment: "hello" },
        headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "multipart/form-data" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

  test "bad room id returns 404 Not Found" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(999_999, @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello"
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "room the bot is not a member of returns 404 Not Found until added" do
    closed_room = rooms(:watercooler)
    assert_not_includes closed_room.users, @bot

    post room_bot_messages_url(closed_room, @bot.bot_key), params: "Hello"

  end

    assert_response :unauthorized

    post room_bot_messages_url(@room, "#{@bot.id}-wrongtoken"), params: "Hello"
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

    end

  end
end

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

module Message::Broadcasts
  def broadcast_create
    broadcast_append_to room, :messages, target: [ room, :messages ]
    broadcast_unread_room
  end

  def broadcast_remove
    broadcast_remove_to room, :messages
  end

  private
    # Fanned out to the room's members rather than published on one global stream, so
    # that the timing of activity in a room only reaches people who are in it.
    def broadcast_unread_room
      room.memberships.pluck(:user_id).each do |user_id|
        ActionCable.server.broadcast UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(user_id), { roomId: room.id }
      end
    end
end

class Message < ApplicationRecord
  include Attachment, Broadcasts, Mentionee, Pagination, Searchable

  belongs_to :room, touch: true
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy

  has_rich_text :body

  before_create -> { self.client_message_id ||= Random.uuid }
  after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:created_at) }
  scope :with_creator, -> { preload(creator: :avatar_attachment) }
  scope :with_attachment_details, -> {
    with_rich_text_body_and_embeds
    with_attached_attachment
      .includes(attachment_blob: :variant_records)
  }
  scope :with_boosts, -> { includes(boosts: :booster) }

  def plain_text_body
    body.to_plain_text.presence || attachment&.filename&.to_s || ""
  end

  def to_key
    [ client_message_id ]
  end

  def content_type
    case
    when attachment?    then "attachment"
    when sound.present? then "sound"
    else                     "text"
    end.inquiry
  end

  def sound
    plain_text_body.match(/\A\/play (?<name>\w+)\z/) do |match|
      Sound.find_by_name match[:name]
    end
  end
end

class ContentFilters::RemoveSoloUnfurledLinkText < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    normalize_tweet_url(solo_unfurled_url) == normalize_tweet_url(content.to_plain_text)
  end

  def apply
    fragment.replace("div") { |node| node.tap { |n| n.inner_html = unfurled_links.first.to_s } }
  end

  private
    TWITTER_DOMAINS = %w[ x.com twitter.com ]
    TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING = { "x.com" => "twitter.com" }

    def solo_unfurled_url
      unfurled_links.first["href"] if unfurled_links.size == 1
    end

    def unfurled_links
      fragment.find_all("action-text-attachment[@content-type='#{ActionText::Attachment::OpengraphEmbed::OPENGRAPH_EMBED_CONTENT_TYPE}']")
    end

    def normalize_tweet_url(url)
      return url unless twitter_url?(url)

      uri = URI.parse(url)

      uri.dup.tap do |u|
        u.host = TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING[uri.host&.downcase] || uri.host
        u.query = nil
      end.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      url
    end

    def twitter_url?(url)
      url.present? && TWITTER_DOMAINS.any? { |domain| url.strip.include?(domain) }
    end
end

**Analyzing the Implementation for Bot Exclusion from Open Rooms**

Okay, let's dive into this feature request, dissecting it bit by bit to ensure a solid implementation. My initial focus is on the current behavior and identifying precisely where the modifications are needed.

First, the requirement: bots shouldn't join open rooms by default, but humans should. I'll need to check the existing code to see how it handles this. Currently, the `User` model's `after_create_commit` callback, `grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, appears to be the primary point of concern. Even more concerning, the tests in `rooms/open_test.rb` implicitly rely on this.

We need to flip that assumption. Our new default should be that bots *don't* join open rooms automatically. The existing tests, then, will need to be refactored. I need to ensure the existing tests verify the *new* default behavior. Then, those tests that specifically *require* the bot to be in a particular room – like those related to webhooks and messages – need to explicitly grant membership using `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` or `@room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)`.

This change necessitates a careful review of our existing test suite. I'm going to carefully trace and understand the technical details of membership insertion, webhook triggering, and how to handle `joined` events.

In a real-world asynchronous queue (like Solid Queue or Resque), if the job fires *before* the transaction commits, the ActiveJob deserialization of the bot or room might encounter data inconsistencies because the membership isn't yet committed.

This then runs `Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(selected_users)`, which creates the `Rooms::Direct` room. Crucially, then `room.memberships.grant_to(users)` runs.       push_subscriptions.delete_all

      sessions.delete_all

    end

  end

module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :bots, -> { active.bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id

    normalizes :webhook_url, with: ->(url) { url.strip.presence }

    validates :name, presence: true, if: :bot?
    validate :webhook_url_must_be_http, if: -> { bot? && webhook_url.present? }

    before_validation :set_bot_defaults, on: :create, if: :bot?

    scope :with_webhook, -> { active.bot.where.not(webhook_url: nil) }
    scope :open_room_members, -> { not_bot.or(bot.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def authenticate_bot(bot_key)
      id, bot_token = bot_key.to_s.split("-", 2)
      return nil if id.blank? || bot_token.blank?

      if bot = active.bot.find_by(id: id)
        bot if bot.bot_token.present? && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(bot.bot_token, bot_token)
      end
    end
  end

  def bot_key
    "#{id}-#{bot_token}" if bot? && bot_token.present?
  end

  private
    def set_bot_defaults
      self.password_digest ||= ""
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      SecureRandom.base58(24)
    end

    def webhook_url_must_be_http
      uri = URI.parse(webhook_url)
      unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
        errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
      end
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
    end
end
EOF

class Membership < ApplicationRecord
  include Connectable

  belongs_to :room
  belongs_to :user

  after_destroy_commit { user.reset_remote_connections }

  enum :involvement, %w[ invisible nothing mentions everything ].index_by(&:itself), prefix: :involved_in

  scope :with_ordered_room, -> { includes(:room).joins(:room).order("LOWER(rooms.name)") }
  scope :without_direct_rooms, -> { joins(:room).where.not(room: { type: "Rooms::Direct" }) }

  scope :visible, -> { where.not(involvement: :invisible) }
  scope :unread,  -> { where.not(unread_at: nil) }

  class << self
    def grant(rows)
      return if rows.blank?

      inserted = insert_all(rows, returning: %i[ room_id user_id ]).rows
      return if inserted.blank?

      deliver_bot_joined_webhooks_later(inserted)
    end

    private
      def deliver_bot_joined_webhooks_later(inserted)
        user_ids = inserted.map(&:last).uniq
        bots_by_id = User.with_webhook.where(id: user_ids).index_by(&:id)
        return if bots_by_id.empty?

        room_ids = inserted.map(&:first).uniq
        rooms_by_id = Room.without_directs.where(id: room_ids).index_by(&:id)
        return if rooms_by_id.empty?

        inserted.each do |room_id, user_id|
          if (room = rooms_by_id[room_id]) && (bot = bots_by_id[user_id])
            Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, event: "joined", room: room)
          end
        end
      end
  end

  def read
    update!(unread_at: nil)
  end

  def unread?\n    unread_at.present?\n  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/room.rb
class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      rows = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }
      Membership.grant(rows)
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_bot_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def deliver_bot_webhooks_later(message)
      message.mentionees.with_webhook.where.not(id: message.creator_id).find_each do |bot|
        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, event: "mention", message: message)
      end
    end
end
EOF

**Rails Callback Gotcha!**

Okay, here's what I'm seeing: I'm looking at `app/models/user.rb`, and immediately I spot a potential Rails gotcha with these callbacks:

My immediate thought is, "Uh oh!" Both callbacks are using the *same* method name, `:grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, but they're attached to different events (`after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit`). Rails' callback system, specifically in ActiveRecord, seems to be deduping the callbacks based on method name, meaning the second one is clobbering the first!  The `if:` condition on the `after_create_commit` call is being completely overwritten by the second, more complex, condition on the `after_update_commit`.  That's a classic Rails trap!

So, the solution is, of course, to avoid the collision by using different method names or a unified callback.  I immediately consider: `after_save_commit` instead, using a single callback to handle both create and update scenarios.  That looks cleaner, anyway.

So, let's look at `after_save_commit` which should be more elegant, with this condition:

    def should_join_open_rooms?
      return false unless active?

Now, let me run through this to see if I'm covering all bases:

1.  **Human user creation:** `previously_new_record? == true`, `active? == true`, `!bot? == true`.  This evaluates to `true`, as it should.
2.  **Human user update:** `previously_new_record? == false`, `bot? == false`.  This evaluates to `false`. Good.
3.  **Bot created, `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`:** `previously_new_record? == true`, `add_to_all_open_rooms? == false`.  This returns `false`, which is correct.
4.  **Bot created, `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`:**  `previously_new_record? == true`, `add_to_all_open_rooms? == true`. This evaluates to `true`.
5.  **Bot updated, `add_to_all_open_rooms` changed from `false` to `true`:** `previously_new_record? == false`, `active? == true`, `bot? == true`, `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) == true`. Evaluates to `true`.  Perfect.
6.  **Bot updated, `add_to_all_open_rooms` changed from `true` to `false`:** `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) == false`. This returns `false`.
7.  **Bot updated (name/webhook_url changed, `add_to_all_open_rooms` unchanged):** `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)` is `false`.  Returns `false`.
8.  **Bot deactivated:** `active?` is `false`. Returns `false`.

Looks good.  Now I need to update `app/models/user.rb` with this `after_save_commit` approach and then re-run `UserTest` and `UsersControllerTest` to make sure everything still works as expected.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_save_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: :should_join_open_rooms?

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      (bot? ? memberships : memberships.without_direct_rooms).delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil, webhook_url: nil, add_to_all_open_rooms: false
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.grant(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id, involvement: "mentions" } })
    end

    def should_join_open_rooms?
      return false unless active?

      if previously_new_record?
        !bot? || add_to_all_open_rooms?
      else
        bot? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true)
      end
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

**A Deep Dive into Webhook Testing and Feature Implementation**

Okay, so I was looking closely at the `webhook_test.rb` file, specifically lines 10-15 and line 98. I was really trying to wrap my head around how the setup and test assertions interact, especially when `add_to_all_open_rooms` is in the mix or when we are granting membership.

If we're enabling `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` or manually adding the bot to a room during setup, and the bot has a `webhook_url`, creating the bot will also enqueue a `joined` webhook job. I realized that the `assert_enqueued_jobs` method within an active job block checks the *delta* of enqueued jobs, not the total count. And calling `grant_to` in setup, again, enqueues another job!

My concern was this: When we test a mention and use `perform_enqueued_jobs`, it could unknowingly execute the `joined` job *from setup*, leading to false positives or test pollution. It would have meant we're testing the 'joined' job along with the mention! That's not what we want.

I looked at the internals of how `assert_enqueued_jobs` and `perform_enqueued_jobs` work, and the crucial point is that `perform_enqueued_jobs` will execute ALL jobs enqueued of that type. To make sure our test assertions are accurate and isolated, the simplest fix is to call `clear_enqueued_jobs` at the end of the `setup` method. This will keep the tests clean and focused on only what we intend. By either granting membership *before* setting the webhook_url OR clearing the jobs, our tests will be more reliable.

That’s a big win!

Now, let's take this newfound clarity and expand our test suite. I need to make sure we've got solid coverage for these new features, so I'm thinking we need tests in the `bot_test.rb`, `bots_controller_test.rb`, `messages_controller_test.rb`, `users_controller_test.rb`, and of course, `webhook_test.rb` files.

So, I'm thinking these are the test cases we need to implement for our bot management:

1.  **`bot_test.rb`:**
    *   Creation: Generate tokens, `add_to_all_open_rooms` defaults, no open room memberships.
    *   `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`: Grant membership to open rooms at creation, not closed or direct rooms.
    *   Enable for existing bots: Grant to existing and newly created open rooms.
    *   Disable for existing bots: Keep existing memberships, don't add to future open rooms.
    *   Deactivation: Reset to false and revoke memberships.
2.  **`open_test.rb`:**
    *   Open room creation: Grant access to humans and bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`, not bots with `false`.
    *   Room Conversion: Similar access rules when converting a closed room to open, including bots with `false` if they are already members.
3.  **`bots_controller_test.rb`:**
    *   `new` form: Ensure checkbox defaults unchecked, with correct label.
    *   `create` (unchecked): Correct `add_to_all_open_rooms` and no room memberships.
    *   `create` (checked): Correct `add_to_all_open_rooms`, join open rooms, enqueue `joined` jobs.
    *   `edit` form: Show the correct checkbox state.
    *   `update` (checked): Add to existing open rooms, enqueue `joined` for only newly added rooms.
    *   `update` (unchecked): Keep current memberships, no future additions.
4.  **`webhook_test.rb`:**
    *   Adding to closed room: Single enqueue for each added room, no double-enqueue on edits.
    *   Creation with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`: Enqueue once per existing open room.
    *   Enabling `add_to_all_open_rooms`: Enqueue once per *newly* joined open room.
    *   New open room: Enqueue once, don't re-enqueue if already a member.
    *   Direct Conversations: NO enqueue of `joined`.

cat <<'EOF' > test/models/user/bot_test.rb
require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot generates a bot token and does not join open rooms by default" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      @bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    assert @bot.bot?
    assert @bot.active?
    assert_not @bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert @bot.bot_token.present?
    assert_equal "#{@bot.id}-#{@bot.bot_token}", @bot.bot_key
    assert_empty @bot.rooms
  end

  test "creating a bot with add_to_all_open_rooms grants membership to all open rooms" do
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      @bot = User.create!(name: "Everyone Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    end

    assert @bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.order(:id).pluck(:id), @bot.rooms.order(:id).pluck(:id)
  end

  test "toggling add_to_all_open_rooms grants open rooms on enable and keeps memberships on disable" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Toggle Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.grant_to(bot)
    assert_equal [ rooms(:watercooler).id ], bot.room_ids

    bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    expected_ids = (Rooms::Open.pluck(:id) + [ rooms(:watercooler).id ]).sort
    assert_equal expected_ids, bot.rooms.reload.order(:id).pluck(:id)

    new_open_room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "New Open", creator: users(:david))
    assert_includes bot.rooms.reload, new_open_room

    bot.update!(add_to_all_open_rooms: false)
    assert_equal (expected_ids + [ new_open_room.id ]).sort, bot.rooms.reload.order(:id).pluck(:id)

    later_open_room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later Open", creator: users(:david))
    assert_not_includes bot.rooms.reload, later_open_room
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new(name: "", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors[:name].any?\n  end

  test "webhook_url is optional, normalized, and validated as http/https" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Hook Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "  ")
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url

    bot.update!(webhook_url: " https://example.com/hook ")
    assert_equal "https://example.com/hook", bot.webhook_url

    bot.update!(webhook_url: "http://127.0.0.1:4567/callback")
    assert_equal "http://127.0.0.1:4567/callback", bot.webhook_url

    bot.update!(webhook_url: "")
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url

    [ "not-a-url", "ftp://example.com/hook", "javascript:alert(1)" ].each do |bad_url|
      bot.webhook_url = bad_url
      assert_not bot.valid?, "Expected #{bad_url} to be invalid"
      assert bot.errors[:webhook_url].any?
    end
  end

  test "authenticate_bot validates active bots with matching key" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "CI Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(bot.bot_key)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{bot.id}-wrongtoken")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("999999-#{bot.bot_token}")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("invalid")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("#{users(:david).id}-")
  end

  test "deactivating a bot revokes memberships and invalidates bot_key and webhook_url while preserving messages" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin), webhook_url: "https://example.com/hook", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    bot_key = bot.bot_key
    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.grant_to(bot)
    message = rooms(:hq).messages.create!(body: "Deployed!", creator: bot)

    bot.deactivate

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_token
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url
    assert_not bot.add_to_all_open_rooms?
    assert_empty bot.memberships
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(bot_key)
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Rooms::OpenTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "grants access to all users after creation" do
    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "My open room with everyone!", creator: users(:david))
    assert_equal User.count, room.users.count
  end

  test "grants access to all users after becoming open" do
    room = rooms(:watercooler).becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    room.save!
    assert_equal User.count, room.users.count
  end

  test "grants access to people and auto-open bots only" do
    default_bot = User.create!(name: "Default Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david))
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Selective Open", creator: users(:david))

    assert_not_includes room.users, default_bot
    assert_includes room.users, auto_bot
    User.active.not_bot.each do |person|
      assert_includes room.users, person
    end
  end

  test "converting closed room to open preserves existing bot members and only adds auto-open bots" do
    member_bot = User.create!(name: "Member Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david))
    other_bot = User.create!(name: "Other Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david))
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    rooms(:watercooler).memberships.grant_to(member_bot)

    room = rooms(:watercooler).becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    room.save!

    assert_includes room.users, member_bot
    assert_includes room.users, auto_bot
    assert_not_includes room.users, other_bot
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > docs/bots.md
# Chat Bots Architecture

## Data Model
Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (`User::Role`), implemented via the `User::Bot` concern:
- `users.bot_token`: unique random token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`) generated on create for bots; `nil` for human users and deactivated bots.
- `users.creator_id`: references the `User` who created the bot, allowing `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` to work uniformly for creators and administrators.
- `users.webhook_url`: optional HTTP/HTTPS URL where the bot receives webhook callbacks. Blank values normalize to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook.
- `users.add_to_all_open_rooms`: boolean (default `false`). Bots do not join open rooms by default; when enabled, the bot is added to all existing open rooms and automatically joins any open room created or converted from closed later. Disabling it keeps existing memberships.
- `bot_key` (`"<id>-<bot_token>"`): the credential displayed in the UI ("Bot code") and used in the messaging API URL. Verified with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Reusing `User` means bots automatically inherit:
  - Opt-in open-room auto-join (`User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open` via `User.open_room_members`)
  - Closed-room membership management (`Rooms::ClosedsController`)
  - `@`-mention autocompletion (`Autocompletable::UsersController`) and `Message#mentionees` resolution
  - Message authorship (`messages.creator_id`), avatars (`User::Avatar`), broadcasts (`Message::Broadcasts`), and push notifications (`Room::MessagePusher`)
- Bots are excluded from human-only surfaces (login, session transfers, account member list, sidebar DM placeholders) via `User.not_bot`.
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, `webhook_url: nil`, and `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`, and removes all memberships while preserving historical messages.

## Routes & Controllers
- `BotsController` (`resources :bots, except: :show`): UI for listing (`/bots`), creating (`/bots/new`), editing (`/bots/:id/edit`), and deleting bots. Linked from `/account/edit` ("Set up chat bots") for all members. The form includes the optional `Webhook URL` field (`bot[webhook_url]`) and the `Add to all open rooms` switch (`bot[add_to_all_open_rooms]`).
- `Bots::MessagesController` (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`): unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint reading raw request body (or `params[:attachment]`) and returning `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`, `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, or `401 Unauthorized`.

## Outbound Webhooks (`Bot::Webhook` & `Bot::WebhookJob`)
- `mention` event: When a message is created (`after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_bot_webhooks_later` finds active, mentioned bots in that room that have a `webhook_url` (excluding `message.creator`) and enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per bot.
  - Payload: `{ event: "mention", author: { id, name }, room: { id, name, reply_to }, message: { id, body: { text, html }, link } }`.
  - `message.body.text` strips only the target bot's own `<action-text-attachment>` mention node(s) using a unique sentinel before converting to plain text, handling both ASCII spaces and ` ` (`\u00A0`) while preserving other users' and bots' `@`-mentions.
- `joined` event: All membership insertions go through `Membership.grant`, which uses `insert_all(..., returning: %i[ room_id user_id ])` so only newly created memberships (never duplicates or already-existing memberships) trigger `Bot::WebhookJob` (`enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true`) for active bots with a `webhook_url` in non-direct rooms (`Room.without_directs`). Direct rooms (`Rooms::Direct`) never trigger `joined`.
  - Payload: `{ event: "joined", room: { id, name, reply_to } }` (`reply_to` is the relative `room_bot_messages_path` for that room & bot).
- Enqueueing per-bot background jobs ensures webhook HTTP calls never block the user or delay other bots.
- Synchronous responses for both `mention` and `joined`:
  - `200` with `text/plain` (HTML-escaped so literal text renders safely) or `text/html` posts the non-blank response body into the room as the bot's message and calls `broadcast_create`.
  - `204` (or other statuses / empty body) posts nothing.
- Outbound webhook URLs intentionally permit `http://` and `https://` on localhost and private networks (unlike `Opengraph::Fetch`) so self-hosted Campfire instances and local integrations/tests can target internal services.
EOF
